source_refs.note: iii) Selective catalytic reduction (SCR): a main subheading of 14.14 Strategies used to reduce air pollution, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 318-318.

blocks.text: SCR is used in diesel engines to remove pollutants from the emission gases. It reduces NOₓ to N₂ and oxidizes CO and hydrocarbons to CO₂ and water vapour using catalysts, such as TiO₂, zeolites, etc.
book_errors: and oxidizes CO and hydrocarbons to CO₂ and water vapour

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: SCR only reduces NOₓ. Urea solution injected into the exhaust gives ammonia, which reduces NOₓ to N₂ and H₂O over catalysts such as V₂O₅/TiO₂ or zeolites. CO and hydrocarbons are oxidised by a separate oxidation catalyst placed before the SCR unit.

blocks.alt: Exhaust after-treatment line. From the Engine, an arrow carries NOx, CO, HC and PM into the Oxidation Catalyst, then a narrow pipe where a blue urea line enters at the Urea Dosing System (a green cone), then a wide can holding the Urea SCR block and the NH3 Oxidate Catalyst block. An arrow leaves with N2, CO2, H2O and PM.
